stories.title: Two dead in rock spire collapse at tourist site in Turkiye's Cappadocia
summary: A landslide triggered by heavy rainfall caused a rock spire to collapse in Turkey’s Cappadocia tourist region on Thursday, killing two people, the local governor said. “We have recovered the bodies of two people who lost their lives.
The incident occurred at 3:15pm local time (5:15pm PKT) when a landslide triggered a rockfall in the town of Goreme near the open-air museum, Kok said.
Eyewitnesses reported hearing a loud noise as the rock spire fell. “Our search and rescue operations at the scene are ongoing.

stories.title: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc on Thursday piled pressure on Israeli Arab leaders over unproven accusations of foreign funding, in a push to neuter parties that could hold the key to forming a government after an inconclusive election.

Israel was nearing the completion of ballot-counting from Tuesday’s election, in which neither Netanyahu nor the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot looked able to secure a majority in the parliament known as the Knesset.
Following Netanyahu’s accusations of impropriety, Ben Gvir went so far as to encourage Israel to “immediately” order the arrests of Arab party leaders.

stories.title: EU hits pause on country-level social media bans for children
summary: The European Union (EU) said on Thursday it does not want any more national-level bans on social media before a pan-European law is approved, as it blocked draft rules put forward by Austria.
Under EU law, member states must notify the European Commission to ensure their bills do not break the bloc’s rules.

Austria wanted to ban children under 14 from social media, but the EU said no. “The commission has decided to postpone for 12 months any draft national laws overlapping with the future harmonised rules,” EU spokesman Thomas Regnier said.

stories.title: 'Not related to defence': Govt responds to Fazl's remarks about Makkah pact countries' meeting in Tehran
summary: Federal ministers on Thursday responded to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s remarks regarding a recent huddle in Tehran comprising the Makkah defence pact countries and Iran.
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the meeting was not related to defence.
He said one should at least show some dignity. ‘Not related to defence’ Meanwhile, in the Senate, Naqvi also responded to Fazl’s remarks on his participation in the Tehran meeting.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral video of JUI-F chief asking for forgiveness in NA is doctored
summary: But you are not doing it.” Another PML-N supporter, based on their bio and past posts, shared the same video with the following caption: “All the antics, today in the assembly, the ripples of apology.

Shahzad Younas Sheikh, who, according to his X bio, is a former spokesperson for Punjab, also shared the video with the caption: “See how Fazlu kept mumbling apologies in the assembly even today, but no one shares this bit of his speech.” The post garnered 661 views.
The claim that a viral video shows JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman asking for forgiveness in the National Assembly is false.

stories.title: 'Absolutely absurd verdict': Lawyers, journalists react to Imaan, Hadi's sentencing in security breach case
summary: This time, the couple was sentenced to 10 years in a security breach case following a jail trial.
Journalist Zarrar Khuhro also pointed out that the couple was sentenced to 10 years for “removing a barrier”. “A decade in jail is what rapists usually get,” he said.
Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha, two human rights lawyers, sentenced to 10 years in prison over road barriers they maintain they never removed.

stories.title: ATC sentences Imaan, Hadi to 10 years in security breach case
summary: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court on Thursday sentenced human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to 10 years in prison each in the security breach case.
Imaan and Hadi were being tried in jail in the 2024 case pertaining to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest.
On Monday, the couple approached the SC to challenge the IHC’s Oct 19 order refusing to stay the trial in the case.

stories.title: Bilawal urges Achakzai to use ‘authority’ delegated by Imran, asks opposition to play role in Parliament
summary: Turning to Achakzai, Bilawal urged the opposition leader to use the “authority and power” delegated to him and the Senate opposition leader by Imran Khan to direct opposition members to participate in committee proceedings and discuss pressing national issues.

Bilawal said that since Parliament had decided, on a motion moved by the PPP, to constitute a committee on electoral reforms, the opposition leader should nominate a representative to the committee and submit the name to the speaker’s office.
The PPP chairman had invited the opposition to join the Parliamentary electoral reforms process and “engage with the federal government”.

stories.title: Polluted priorities
summary: Last year, disruptions to Punjab’s air monitoring network raised suspicions that pollution levels were being hidden; officials cited technical faults.
A temporary improvement at a pollution hotspot, or near a monitoring station, cannot prove that the city’s air is becoming safer.
Punjab officials say easterly winds have been bringing polluted air from India into Lahore.

stories.title: Obama mocks Trump’s government-wide response to Cheesecake Factory remark ahead of US midterms
summary: Neither man is on the ballot, but Republican President Trump and Democratic former president Obama took prominent roles on the campaign trail on Wednesday, with less than a week to go before congressional races that could shift the balance of power in Washington.
On Wednesday, Obama appeared in Morrow, Georgia, near Atlanta, where he urged voters to support Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff, who faces a challenge from Representative Mike Collins, a Republican.

In Michigan, where Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed are locked in a tight race for the Senate seat being vacated by Democratic Senator Gary Peters, both campaigns are relying on high-profile allies to energise supporters and boost turnout.

stories.title: Pakistan, China sign agreement to operationalise green channel at Sost-Khunjerab border
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and China have signed an agreement to operationalise a green channel at the Sost-Khunjerab border for agricultural and allied products to facilitate bilateral trade.
The agreement also provides for enhanced exchange of information and risk alerts between the two customs administrations to strengthen coordination and improve the management of cross-border trade.
The operationalisation of the green channel is expected to improve the efficiency of agricultural trade and strengthen customs cooperation between the two countries.

stories.title: Lahore ranks world’s most polluted major city as Punjab battles poor air quality
summary: LAHORE: Lahore was ranked the world’s most polluted major city on Thursday, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 419, as air pollution levels remained high across Punjab ahead of the peak smog season.

Punjab government’s air quality monitoring dashboard shows hazardous pollution levels in several cities. — Screengrab via AQI Punjab Both, however, indicated elevated pollution levels in Lahore and other parts of Punjab.

As pollution levels remained high, the Punjab government intensified enforcement against sources of emissions, including smoke-emitting vehicles, brick kilns, industrial units, plastic burning and construction dust.

stories.title: Death toll from Thar ambulance fire rises to nine: district official
summary: The incident occurred on Wednesday night when an oxygen cylinder exploded in an ambulance at a Peoples Primary Healthcare Initiative (PPHI)-run hospital in the Dano Dhandhal area of Nagarparkar taluka.
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Thursday announced compensation of Rs2 million each for the families of the nine people killed in the incident.
He also ordered a transparent inquiry into the incident and directed PPP MPA Qasim Soomro to travel to Nagarparkar to oversee relief efforts.

stories.title: Australia lead by 100 after Inglis century
summary: Josh Inglis completed his century before Australia were bowled out for 429 – a first innings lead of 100 – on the third day of the third Test against South Africa at Newlands on Thursday.
Inglis reached his century off 132 balls when he reverse-swept off-spinner Simon Harmer for four but he was caught behind off the same bowler three balls later.
Carey was caught at slip off Harmer four overs later.

stories.title: TikTok removes 23.2m videos in Pakistan in Q2
summary: TikTok removed more than 23.2 million videos in Pakistan for violating its community guidelines between April and June 2026, with nearly 95% of the content taken down within 24 hours of being posted, according to the platform’s latest enforcement report.

The short-video sharing platform removed 23,243,711 videos in Pakistan during the second quarter of 2026, while the global tally exceeded 188.2 million, according to TikTok’s Q2 Community Guidelines Enforcement Report released on Thursday.
TikTok said its quarterly enforcement report provides an overview of its content moderation efforts, including video removals, account enforcement and the use of automated detection systems.

stories.title: Pillion riding banned in KP's Bajaur for 10 days owing to security situation
summary: BAJAUR: The district administration banned pillion riding in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur for 10 days on Thursday by invoking Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) owing to the security situation.
Given the prevailing security situation and the possible use of motorcycles in terrorist activities, there was a need for immediate preventive measures, the notification added.
Earlier, the authorities imposed a 15-day ban on pillion riding in Bajaur on September 5, citing the security situation back then as well.

stories.title: Afghanistan opium poppy cultivation surges despite Taliban govt ban: UN
summary: Opium poppy cultivation in Afghanistan more than quadrupled in 2026 despite a Taliban government ban, the United Nations said on Thursday, urging that impoverished farmers needed alternatives to the lucrative crop.

This photograph taken on June 22, 2026 shows Afghan farmers harvesting sap from poppies in a field in Badakhshan province. — AFP Afghanistan’s 2022 crackdown drove cultivated areas down from more than 200,000 hectares to 10,000 hectares in 2025.
Mohammad lives with his parents in Badakhshan, which has become Afghanistan’s main opium poppy-growing province. “The Taliban threaten us and do not allow us to grow opium.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz approves expansion of Karachi, Lahore airports
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday approved the expansion of Karachi and Lahore airports under their respective master plans, directing authorities to complete the projects within the stipulated timelines and ensure compliance with international standards.

Officials told the prime minister that the runway expansion at Karachi’s Jinnah International Airport had been completed. “During the past year, the CAA activated 14 airports to restore domestic flights,” the statement said.

In February, the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) announced a Rs100 billion expansion plan for Karachi’s Jinnah International Airport, including a new terminal building, a modern cargo village and other facilities to meet rising passenger demand.

stories.title: Osaka vows to return stronger after Tokyo exit
summary: Former world number one Naomi Osaka said she would "keep attempting" to get back to her Grand Slam-winning best after her season ended with a second-round exit in Japan on Thursday.
The four-time Grand Slam champion lost 6-3, 7-5 to Slovakian 18-year-old Mia Pohankova, ranked 144 in the world, at the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo.
"But if you're asking me how I think my tennis is, I think it's pretty good." Osaka was appearing at the Pan Pacific Open for the first time in four years.

stories.title: Singapore foreign minister to undertake official visit to Pakistan on Oct 30
summary: During the visit, Dar and Dr Balakrishnan will hold bilateral talks covering the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Singapore relations and exchange views on regional and global developments of mutual interest, it added.
Balakrishnan will also call on Pakistan’s leadership, the FO said.
Pakistan and Singapore maintain cordial bilateral relations based on mutual respect and longstanding friendship.

stories.title: Warrican leads West Indies fightback
summary: West Indies spinner Jomel Warrican took five wickets to bowl Bangladesh out for 272 before the visitors reached 134-4 on the second day of the opening Test on Thursday.
Warrican, a left-arm spinner who struck twice on day one, returned figures of 5-53, his fourth five-wicket haul in Test cricket.
Chanderpaul and Greaves helped West Indies recover before bad light brought an early end to the day's play

stories.title: Bayern cruise into German Cup last 16
summary: Newly-crowned Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane was left on the bench as Bayern Munich sailed to a 6-1 win over second-tier Magdeburg in the German Cup last 32 on Wednesday.
Olise returned the favour by setting up Saibari midway through the opening half and added a third from the spot early in the second half, with regular penalty-taker Kane still on the bench.
Earlier on Wednesday, Germany forward Deniz Undav's 90th-minute strike took Stuttgart to a 1-0 win at 10-man Paderborn.

stories.title: Two children killed, 13 injured as wedding bus collides with tractor-trolley in Peshawar
summary: Two children were killed and 13 people, including women and children, were injured when a bus carrying wedding guests collided with a tractor-trolley in the Safen area of Budh Bher, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), Rescue 1122 said on Thursday.
According to the rescue service, its Peshawar control room dispatched four ambulances and medical teams to the site shortly after receiving information about the accident.

Rescue 1122 Spokesperson Bilal Ahmad Faizi said rescue service personnel provided first aid to 15 injured people at the scene, while eight of them, including women and children, were shifted to hospital for further treatment.

stories.title: At least 5 killed, over two dozen injured as bus plunges into drain in Punjab's Hafizabad
summary: LAHORE: At least five people were killed and 27 others injured when a passenger bus plunged into a drain in Punjab’s Hafizabad district on Thursday, according to Rescue 1122.
Five rescue vehicles participated in the operation, Rescue 1122 said.

The accident occurred two days after 10 people were killed and 44 others injured when a passenger bus overturned after hitting a road divider in Rajanpur district’s Rojhan tehsil on the Indus Highway on Wednesday.

stories.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia discuss investment in agriculture, minerals and mining
summary: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia discussed expanding economic cooperation in agriculture, minerals and mining, and other sectors with investment potential, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of Finance on Thursday.
Aurangzeb reaffirmed the longstanding friendship between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia and appreciated Riyadh’s continued support for Islamabad.

Cooperation in agriculture, minerals and mining, alongside efforts to maintain a predictable investment environment, remains central to Pakistan’s drive to attract Saudi capital and support sustainable economic growth.

stories.title: Punjab govt has 1m tonnes of wheat for five months, provincial assembly told
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab Assembly was told on Wednesday that the provincial government had over one million tonnes of wheat in stock for the next five months as opposition members raised concerns over rising flour prices, delayed development funds and the plight of farmers.
More than 1.5m bags of wheat arrived in Punjab markets daily, while the government had over 1m tonnes of grain in stock to meet requirements for the next five months, she told the house.

Replying to a question by treasury member Amjad Ali Javed, the food minister said the government had cancelled the licences of 90 out of 185 private markets following complaints of fraud against citizens in the name of such markets.

stories.title: Fake MoFA official arrested in Gujrat
summary: GUJRAT: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) claimed on Wednesday to have arrested a fake official of the Foreign Affairs Liaison Office (FALO), Gujrat, when he was allegedly demanding bribes from the applicants for the attestation of their documents.
An FIA official said that the role of other agents, Gujrat officials of MoFA and other departments would also be probed during the investigation.

Earlier, in March this year, the MoFA had removed the head of Gujrat FALO and two other officials on the complaints of corruption in the attestation of documents after a junior official lodged a case of Rs4 million theft at his flat located near the office.

stories.title: Punjab CM announces establishment of Apna Kisan Bank
summary: LAHORE: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Wednesday announced the establishment of the province’s first ‘Apna Kisan Bank’ and agricultural loans worth Rs17 billion and an increase in financing under the Kisan Card scheme.
Farmers can get loans up to Rs50m at 5pc markup; Kisan Card limit increased The CM said the Rs17bn in subsidised loans would benefit farmers cultivating around five million acres.
She said the government had resisted pressure to impose agricultural income tax on farmers and was committed to protecting their interests.

stories.title: Turkish Maarif Foundation: Lahore High Court sets aside labour court order
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) has set aside orders of a labour court and a wages authority against the Turkish Maarif Foundation in a claim filed by a former vice-principal.
The Wages Authority awarded her Rs10.8 million, and the labour court dismissed the foundation’s appeal for non-appearance and non-deposit of the decreed amount.

Justice Hassan directed the authority to decide the matter afresh, especially the preliminary issues, in light of the case’s background, Pakistan-Turkiye relations and the foundation’s legal status as recognised in the Supreme Court’s judgement of December 2018.

stories.title: 294 Sahiwal farmers booked for water theft in five months
summary: At Chak 63/5-L, a farmer, Sadiq, allegedly broke a water outlet (moga) and diverted irrigation water to his fields and those of other shareholders.

At Chak 66/5-L, also known as Katorwala, 15 people, including Iqrar, Yaseen, Alam Sher, Jahan Khan, Muhammad Iqbal, Manzoor Ahmed, Zahoor Ahmed, Talib, Altaf, Amjad, Ghulam Fareed, Furqan and Khalid, allegedly broke a water outlet and diverted water to their fields.

At Chak 48/5-L, 13 people, including Muhammad Sharif, Zulfiqar, Hanif, Mushtaq Ahmed, Sardar, Akhtar Ali, Zahid, Anwar, Iqbal, Amjad, Sarwar and Manzoor, were accused of illegally diverting irrigation water to their fields.

stories.title: Inquiry holds school owner responsible for roof collapse
summary: PESHAWAR: An inquiry into the recent deadly collapse of a school roof here has held the owner responsible for using substandard construction material.
On Wednesday, the inquiry committee held the school owner responsible for using substandard construction material.
The meeting, chaired by the governor, was also briefed about negligence by the relevant departments.

stories.title: Child’s kidnapping, murder suspects killed in ‘encounter’ in Muridke
summary: TOBA TEK SINGH: Police claimed that two suspects in a kidnapping for ransom and murder of a five-year-old boy were killed in an encounter late on Tuesday night.
Police claimed the attackers attempted to free the suspects and during the exchange of fire, both the detained suspects sustained injuries and died on the spot.

Police claimed that on Tuesday night, the body of the missing child was recovered from the village’s pond on the suspects’ lead, who had allegedly weighed down the sack by putting bricks in it so that the body could not float.

stories.title: Demolition of pre-partition building in Hyderabad stopped
summary: HYDERABAD: The district administration on Monday intervened to stop demolition of a building — recommended for inclusion in the list of heritage sites — soon after the process was started.
The notice informed him that the building was recommended for inclusion in the list of heritage sites and a decision to this effect was to be taken by the relevant department.
The decision on culture department’s recommendation for inclusion of the property or otherwise in protected heritage list was not taken.

stories.title: Karachi man guns down two sisters for ‘using TikTok’
summary: KARACHI: Two young sisters were allegedly shot dead by their brother over their use of social media in Drigh Road, within the jurisdiction of Shah Faisal Colony police, on Wednesday, police said.
Firing on under-construction building leaves watchman dead A watchman was gunned down and two labourers were wounded in an armed attack on an under-construction building in the Garden area.
The Soldier Bazaar police said two armed men riding a motorcycle resorted to indiscriminate firing on the under-construction Jumani Square located on Nishter Road near Alibhai Auditorium.

stories.title: Court rejects plea to add murder, terrorism charges in Karachi's Gul Plaza fire case
summary: KARACHI: Rejecting an application seeking the addition of murder and terrorism charges, a judicial magistrate accepted the charge sheet in the Gul Plaza fire case on Wednesday, in which the police blamed the building management’s “negligence”.
Judicial Magistrate (South) Aasim Aslam pronounced his order on Wednesday, in which he accepted the final charge sheet filed by the second investigating officer of the case.

The IO chargesheeted four members of Gul Plaza Management Committee — Tanveer Pasta, Amar Ismail, Muhammad Ramazan and Muhammad Ameen — and the owner of an artificial flower shop, Naimatullah, and his over 11-year-old son Huzaifa in the case.

stories.title: Islamabad's Capital Development Authority to start Shahdara Dam project soon
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Wednesday announced that construction of the Shahdara Dam project would begin soon.

The water demand of Islamabad is around 250 million gallons per day (MGD), while the CDA supplies approximately 70 MGD, mostly to the urban population, through three main sources, including Khanpur Dam, Simly Dam and tubewells.

Meanwhile, every year during the monsoon, the CDA releases large quantities of water from Simly Dam, while Rawalpindi authorities also release water from Rawal Dam, which is located in Islamabad but supplies water to the city’s residents.

stories.title: PSX extends rally to fourth session, gains 1,456 points
summary: The KSE-100 Index extended its winning streak to a fourth consecutive session on Thursday, closing over 167,190 points after gaining about 1,460 points, with roughly 366 million shares changing hands.
The market maintained its positive momentum, extending its winning streak to four consecutive sessions.
Corporate earnings continue to drive market sentiment, with better-than-expected results supporting buying interest in heavyweight stocks.
